description: GPT-3 defines few-shot foundation models. Scaling laws, ViT, CLIP precursors, AlphaFold 2 solving protein folding, and RLHF breakthroughs set up ChatGPT. Timnit Gebru's firing exposes ethics tensions.

events.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
events.summary: Jared Kaplan et al. showed test loss scales as a smooth power-law in parameters, data and compute over 7+ orders of magnitude, with architecture shape mattering little. It established larger models are far more sample-efficient and compute-optimal training means training very large models. It directly motivated GPT-3 and the entire scale-up race.
events.significance: The engineer's handbook for the LLM race; cited in every scaling decision to 2024.

events.title: Meena human-like open-domain chatbot
events.summary: Google unveiled Meena, a 2.6B Evolved Transformer seq2seq trained on 40B words of social media, plus Sensibleness and Specificity Average (SSA). Meena scored 72% SSA versus 86% human, far above Mitsuku and DialoGPT. It set the template for chatbot evaluation and was the direct predecessor to LaMDA.
events.significance: Google's dialogue track that leads to LaMDA, Bard and Gemini.

events.title: SimCLR contrastive learning for vision
events.summary: Chen et al. simplified contrastive self-supervised vision learning to strong augmentations, a learnable projection head and very large batches. A linear probe on ResNet-50 reached 76.5% ImageNet top-1, matching supervised training. It ignited the 2020-2021 contrastive wave: MoCo v2, BYOL, SwAV, DINO.
events.significance: Self-supervised vision parallel to BERT for language.

events.title: Turing-NLG 17B largest LM at the time
events.summary: Microsoft announced Turing Natural Language Generation at 17B parameters, the largest published LM at the time, beating GPT-2 1.5B on LAMBADA and WikiText-103. Built with Megatron model-parallelism and DeepSpeed on DGX-2s, it opened the 2020 parameter arms race and showcased the Azure supercomputer stack.

events.title: NeRF neural radiance fields for view synthesis
events.summary: Mildenhall et al. optimized a simple MLP mapping 5D coordinates to density plus RGB, rendered with differentiable volume rendering. From only sparse posed images it produced photorealistic novel views far beyond prior neural rendering. Oral plus Best Paper Honorable Mention at ECCV 2020, it spawned Instant-NGP and 3D generation.
events.significance: Founded neural 3D rendering, later combined with diffusion for text-to-3D.

events.title: Agent57 first agent to beat all 57 Atari games
events.summary: Agent57, an evolution of R2D2 and NGU with adaptive exploration-exploitation, became the first agent to surpass human baseline on all 57 Atari games. It closed the Atari benchmark as a grand challenge and shifted DeepMind focus to MuZero-style planning.
events.significance: Closed the ALE benchmark opened by DQN in 2013.

events.title: BlenderBot open-domain chatbot from Facebook
events.summary: Facebook open-sourced Blender, blending empathy, knowledge and personality via Blended Skill Talk fine-tuning in 90M, 2.7B and 9.4B variants. Human evaluators preferred the best Blender over Google Meena 75% for engagingness. It set the open-chatbot SOTA and foreshadowed BlenderBot 2.0 with memory and search.

events.title: Jukebox generative model for music with singing
events.summary: Jukebox generated raw-audio music with rudimentary singing by compressing waveforms with multi-scale VQ-VAE and modeling codes with Transformers, conditioned on artist and genre. Trained on 1.2M songs, it could produce multi-minute pastiches. Released with weights and samples, it was the WaveNet-era apex and raised copyright questions later litigated for Suno and Udio.
events.significance: Early warning of generative music copyright fights.

events.title: RAG retrieval-augmented generation
events.summary: Lewis et al. combined a Dense Passage Retriever over Wikipedia with a BART generator, marginalizing over retrieved docs to produce answers with provenance. It set SOTA on Natural Questions, TriviaQA and FEVER without storing all knowledge in weights. It pioneered retrieval-LMs later realized in modern RAG systems.
events.significance: Architectural ancestor of every 2023-2024 RAG product and SearchGPT.

events.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
events.summary: OpenAI published the 175B-parameter autoregressive Transformer GPT-3, 10x larger than any prior dense LM, showing task-agnostic few and zero-shot performance via in-context prompting rivaling fine-tuned SOTA on translation, QA and arithmetic with no gradient updates. Posted May 28, presented at NeurIPS 2020, it defined the foundation-model era and documented misuse and bias risks.
events.significance: Model that created the foundation-model concept and startup ecosystem.

events.title: OpenAI API private beta (first commercial GPT-3 product)
events.summary: OpenAI launched its API in private beta as a general-purpose text-in text-out interface powered by the GPT-3 family, its first commercial product after capped-profit restructuring. Tens of thousands applied; early demos like AI Dungeon and copywriting went viral in July. It established controlled API access over open weights as OpenAI's deployment model.
events.significance: Business-model pivot from research lab to API platform.

events.title: GPT-3 hype wave: AI Dungeon and copywriting demos go viral
events.summary: In July 2020 after API beta, demos like AI Dungeon, GPT-3 copywriting and code generation went viral, prompting Sam Altman's hype is way too much caution. It established the pattern of viral LLM demos driving funding and criticism that repeats with Copilot, ChatGPT and Sora.
events.significance: Cultural moment when the public first saw few-shot prompting.

events.title: DDPM denoising diffusion probabilistic models
events.summary: Jonathan Ho et al. showed diffusion models trained on a weighted variational bound could generate high-quality images, reaching FID 3.17 on CIFAR-10 and ProgressiveGAN parity on LSUN. Posted June 19, NeurIPS 2020 poster, it revived diffusion and directly enabled GLIDE, DALL-E 2 and Stable Diffusion.
events.significance: Technical seed of the entire 2022 image boom.

events.title: wav2vec 2.0 self-supervised speech representations
events.summary: Baevski et al. learned from raw audio alone via CNN encoder plus masked Transformer solving a contrastive task, then fine-tuned on tiny labeled data. It achieved 1.8% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean and beat prior SOTA with 100x less labeled data. It did for speech what BERT did for text and underpinned HuBERT and Whisper-era work.
events.significance: Foundation for modern self-supervised speech.

events.summary: Formed in July 2020 as a Discord to replicate GPT-3 openly after OpenAI kept weights private, EleutherAI grew into a nonprofit institute. It produced The Pile, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX and LM Eval Harness. Its founding marks the start of the open LLM movement culminating in BLOOM and Llama.

events.title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback (RLHF breakthrough)
events.summary: OpenAI scaled RLHF (reward model from 64k human summary comparisons plus PPO) to show 6.7B human-feedback models beat 10x larger supervised models and even human references, transferring zero-shot to news summarization. Blog Sept 4, arXiv Sept 9, NeurIPS 2020, it was the key RLHF proof-point and direct ancestor of InstructGPT and ChatGPT.
events.significance: Method that makes ChatGPT helpful and safe enough to ship.

events.summary: Waymo One removed safety drivers for public rider-only minivan rides in Chandler and Phoenix, the first true robotaxi service at scale. It leapt ahead of Cruise and Uber ATG and contrasted Tesla's supervised FSD approach. It validated lidar plus HD-map autonomy while sparking cost and scaling debates.
events.significance: First real driverless taxi service, autonomy counterpoint to LLMs.

events.title: Vision Transformer (ViT): An Image is Worth 16x16 Words
events.summary: Dosovitskiy et al. applied pure Transformer encoders to 16x16 image patches, showing pretraining on JFT-300M lets it beat SOTA CNNs with far less compute (88.55% ImageNet). Posted Oct 22, ICLR 2021, it proved minimal vision inductive bias works at scale and triggered DeiT, Swin, DINO and MAE.
events.significance: Transformer conquers vision; CNN dominance ends.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 wins CASP14 by landslide (protein folding solved)
events.summary: At CASP14, DeepMind revealed AlphaFold 2 scored median GDT_TS 92.4 with 87 of 92 domains high-accuracy versus 75 for next best. Based on the novel Evoformer plus structure module, coordinators declared the 50-year grand challenge largely solved for single chains. It set up July 2021 open source and database releases and the 2024 Nobel Prize.
events.significance: First AI solution to a 50-year biology grand challenge.

events.title: Timnit Gebru forced out of Google
events.summary: Co-lead of Ethical AI Timnit Gebru was fired after dispute over retracting the Stochastic Parrots large-LM risks paper and an email criticizing diversity and censorship. One of few Black women in the field and Gender Shades author, her exit drew 1200+ Googler and 1500+ academic signatures and NLRB scrutiny. It exposed corporate control of AI ethics research and led to Mitchell's firing.
events.significance: Fracture between Big Tech and AI ethics that still shapes safety discourse.

events.title: MuZero published in Nature
events.summary: The Nature version formalized MuZero learning only reward, policy and value predictions for MCTS planning without knowing rules. It matched AlphaZero superhuman in Go, chess and shogi and set SOTA on 57 Atari games. It proved model-based planning works in visually complex domains.
events.significance: Generalized AlphaZero to unknown dynamics, bridge to real-world planning.

events.summary: EleutherAI released The Pile (825 GiB, 22 subsets: Pile-CC, PubMed, Books3, GitHub, arXiv, StackExchange) with paper 2101.00027. It showed Pile-trained models improve cross-domain generalization. It powered GPT-Neo and GPT-J and became the open alternative to WebText and C4.
events.significance: Dataset backbone of the first open GPT-3 replicas.
